project.name: fwupd

The line anchors below are resolved against that staged vulnerable tree, which matches the saved ASan frames in `libfwupdplugin/fu-coswid-firmware.c` at lines 410, 433, 520, and 609, `libfwupdplugin/fu-coswid-common.c` at line 361, and `libfwupdplugin/fu-uswid-firmware.c` at line 159.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42534794 (fwupd): Heap-buffer-overflow WRITE 4 found by fuzz target uswid_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42534794
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / reproduction_report.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source in `/src/fwupd` / staged `poc` bytes decoded locally
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 4` in `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_entity` while `uswid_fuzzer` processed the exact staged 4066-byte witness with SHA-256 `dba2f8d9e57b4ca359983e7af9e179455622a48518c9461dce60d0e634f57572`. `fu_uswid_firmware_parse()` reaches `fu_coswid_firmware_parse()` on attacker-controlled bytes at line 159, and line 520 materializes the first CBOR object from that slice. Offline CBOR inspection of the witness shows that object is a one-pair root map keyed by `ENTITY` whose value is an 18-element array; the last entity map has 647 key/value pairs and contains 11 interleaved scalar `ROLE` pairs `33:24` (raw bytes `18 21 18 18`). `fu_coswid_firmware_parse()` selects that `ENTITY` field at lines 608-609, `fu_coswid_parse_one_or_many()` iterates the array and passes the 18th map into `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_entity()`, and that function allocates a `FuCoswidFirmwareEntity` with `FuCoswidEntityRole roles[6]`. Each repeated scalar role pair takes the unguarded scalar branch and executes `entity->roles[entity_role_cnt++] = role`; after six successful stores, the seventh repeated scalar role writes 4 bytes to `entity->roles[6]`, exactly 0 bytes past the 40-byte heap allocation, matching the saved ASan heap-buffer-overflow write. The fix replaces the append array with a bitfield and validates role values before setting bits, so this witness no longer reaches the overflowing store.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the attacker-controlled bytes handed from the outer uSWID parser into the CBOR object graph later walked by `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_entity`.
source.value_from: The staged 4066-byte `gt_results/arvo_42534794/poc` has SHA-256 `dba2f8d9e57b4ca359983e7af9e179455622a48518c9461dce60d0e634f57572`. Offline CBOR inspection of the witness shows that the first parsed object materialized here is a one-pair root map keyed by `ENTITY` whose value is an 18-element array; its last entity map has 647 key/value pairs, including 11 interleaved scalar `ROLE` pairs `33:24` (`18 21 18 18`). That first CBOR object spans 3291 bytes, leaving trailing bytes in the passed slice, which matches source recording `result.read` at line 530 rather than assuming the whole slice was consumed.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: In the crashing entity map, each repeated `ROLE` field arrives as a scalar CBOR uint 24 rather than as an array. That repeated scalar shape is the attacker-controlled state that keeps the parser on the unguarded scalar append path for each of the 11 repeated `ROLE` pairs.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: Offline CBOR inspection of the last entity map shows 11 interleaved key/value pairs `33:24` (`18 21 18 18`) at pair indices 15, 63, 125, 203, 251, 314, 346, 368, 416, 483, and 594.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The scalar `ROLE` branch appends directly into `entity->roles` without the `entity_role_cnt < G_N_ELEMENTS(entity->roles)` check that exists only in the array branch, so repeated scalar role fields can drive the counter past the six-entry buffer.
root_cause.note: For the witnessed entity, the first six scalar role pairs execute this store successfully and leave `entity_role_cnt == 6`; the array branch at lines 434-452 is the only place that would reject excess roles, and the patch removes this counter-based append by switching to a checked bitfield.

sink.description: Seventh execution of the same append writes `role` to `entity->roles[6]`, 4 bytes past the six-element heap array inside `FuCoswidFirmwareEntity`.
sink.note: AddressSanitizer reports `WRITE of size 4` at this exact line and says the target address is 0 bytes to the right of the 40-byte heap region allocated for `entity` at line 410.

parser_admitted.description: The outer uSWID parser reaches the inner coSWID parser on attacker-controlled bytes here; the saved ASan stack includes this call immediately before `fu_coswid_firmware_parse`.

fine_trace.note: Source step. This call materializes the first CBOR object from the attacker-controlled slice handed in by the outer uSWID parser. In the exact witness that object is a one-pair root map whose key is `2` (`FU_COSWID_TAG_ENTITY`) and whose value is an 18-element array; the last element is a 647-pair entity map containing 11 interleaved scalar `ROLE` pairs `33:24`.

In the root-map loop, `fu_coswid_read_tag()` decodes the sole root key from step 1 as `FU_COSWID_TAG_ENTITY`, so `pairs[i].value` is the 18-element entity array and becomes the value forwarded to `fu_coswid_parse_one_or_many()` at line 609.

Because the forwarded `ENTITY` value is an array, the helper iterates it. On `j == 17`, `value` is the last entity map from step 1; `cbor_isa_map(value)` succeeds and line 361 calls `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_entity(value, ...)` on that exact map.

For that selected entity map, `g_new0` allocates a zeroed `FuCoswidFirmwareEntity`. In vulnerable source this object has only `FuCoswidEntityRole roles[6]` for role storage, and the local append counter `entity_role_cnt` starts at 0.

While iterating the 647 pairs in the selected entity map, 11 interleaved pairs have key 33 and scalar value 24. Each time the key decodes to `FU_COSWID_TAG_ROLE`, control enters this block with `pairs[i].value` still that attacker-supplied scalar.

For each of those 11 `ROLE` entries, `pairs[i].value` is a CBOR uint, so this condition is true and the parser takes the scalar branch. The separate array branch at lines 434-452, which contains the only `entity_role_cnt >= G_N_ELEMENTS(entity->roles)` check, is skipped.
The scalar branch materializes role value 24 from each repeated pair. Vulnerable code accepts that raw uint as `FuCoswidEntityRole` without any range validation before storing it.

With the scalar branch selected, the first six executions of this store fill `entity->roles[0]` through `entity->roles[5]` and advance `entity_role_cnt` from 0 to 6. Nothing in this branch checks the six-slot extent allocated in step 4.

On the seventh repeated scalar `ROLE` pair, `entity_role_cnt` is already 6, so the same store writes `role` to `entity->roles[6]`. `FuCoswidFirmwareEntity` is only 40 bytes, so this 4-byte enum write lands exactly at the end of the heap allocation and ASan reports the saved heap-buffer-overflow write.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: The saved ASan top frame is `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_entity` at line 433, and fine-trace step 9 is that exact overflowing store.
cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes at object level. The allocation stack's `g_new0` call at line 410 creates the same `FuCoswidFirmwareEntity` whose six-slot `roles` array fine-trace step 9 overruns.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run feeds the exact staged 4066-byte witness with SHA-256 `dba2f8d9e57b4ca359983e7af9e179455622a48518c9461dce60d0e634f57572` to `uswid_fuzzer`; once fwupd reaches the root `ENTITY` array, the last entity map contains 11 interleaved scalar `ROLE` pairs `33:24`, and the seventh append at `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_entity:433` overruns `entity->roles`.

format.name: uSWID blob with embedded coSWID ENTITY array
format.contract: The witnessed trigger is the exact 4066-byte file with SHA-256 `dba2f8d9e57b4ca359983e7af9e179455622a48518c9461dce60d0e634f57572`. The first CBOR object materialized by `fu_coswid_firmware_parse()` is a root map whose `ENTITY` field contains an 18-element array; its last entity map contains 11 interleaved scalar `ROLE` pairs `33:24` (CBOR bytes `18 21 18 18`). That repeated scalar-role entity shape is what drives `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_entity()` through the unguarded scalar branch six times and makes the seventh append write `entity->roles[6]`. This GT does not generalize beyond that witnessed repeated-scalar-role entity shape.
